shortlist.label: Crohn disease-associated ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has biopsy-proven Crohn disease and is experiencing ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Infliximab-induced ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was initially on infliximab therapy, which is a known cause of ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse, and adalimumab is also a known cause of ocular inflammation

shortlist.label: Blepharitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has bilateral scaly, thickened, and erythematous eyelids with crusty plaques on the eyelid margins, consistent with blepharitis

shortlist.label: Sjögren's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has autoimmune disease (Crohn disease) and is experiencing ocular inflammation, which are risk factors for Sjögren's syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient's ocular symptoms started while on infliximab therapy and switched to adalimumab due to disease relapse, suggesting a possible association with TNF-α inhibitor treatment, and the provided images show resolution after treatment discontinuation.

rejected.label: Crohn disease-associated ocular inflammation
rejected.why: While Crohn disease can cause ocular inflammation, the temporal relationship with infliximab therapy and improvement after discontinuation points more towards a drug-induced cause.

rejected.label: Adalimumab-induced ocular inflammation
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms were present before switching to adalimumab, making infliximab a more likely culprit.

rejected.label: Blepharitis
rejected.why: While the patient has symptoms consistent with blepharitis, such as crusty plaques and erythematous eyelids, the context of TNF-α inhibitor use and the specific pattern of symptoms suggest a drug-induced cause.

rejected.label: Sjögren's syndrome
rejected.why: There is no mention of systemic symptoms or other criteria that would suggest Sjögren's syndrome, making it less likely than a drug-induced cause.

gold: Drug-induced blepharitis and ectropion associated with TNF-α inhibitors (infliximab and adalimumab)
